name: Hiyashi Chuka (Cold Ramen) With Shrimp, Ham, and Vegetables

ingredients.name: cooked corn
ingredients.prep: kernels sliced off and cob discarded

instructions.primary_message: Shell and devein the shrimp. Slice off the kernels of the cooked corn, then discard the cob. Beat the egg. Cut the sliced cooked ham into strips. Shred the imitation crab meat into thin strips. Halve and thinly slice the tomato.
instructions.secondary_message:
0.11 kg shrimp, large
⅔ cup cooked corn
1 egg
0.11 kg sliced cooked ham
4 sticks imitation crab meat
1 large tomato

instructions.primary_message: In a large pot of salted boiling water, cook ramen noodles until tender and springy. Drain in a colander, rinse under cold running water, and let drip dry. Set aside. (If they being to clump or stick, run under cold water again to loosen.)
Meanwhile, in a small mixing bowl, stir together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, water, grated ginger, sesame oil, hot oil, and toasted sesame seeds. Set dressing aside in the refrigerator to chill.
In a saucepan of simmering salted water, poach shrimp until just cooked through, about 3 minutes. Chill under cold running water, then slice in half lengthwise.

In a small nonstick skillet, cook beaten egg over medium heat until set in a thin sheet like an omelette, about 3 minutes; cover during last minute to set the top. Remove from skillet, let cool 1 minute, then roll and thinly slice into strips.

To serve, place chilled drained noodles in serving bowls. Top the noodle with shrimp, corn, scallion, ham, tomato, crab stick, and sliced egg. Add a dollop of hot Japanese mustard in the middle. Divide dressing into 4 small bowls and serve. To eat, pour dressing on top of the noodles at the table, toss to combine, and enjoy right away.

missing: imitation crab meat, shredded into thin strips

description: When the heat starts to climb, I try to use my oven as little as possible. One of my favorite chilled meals: hiyashi chuka, chilled ramen topped all sorts of goodies and tossed in a bright, simple dressing.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Spicy Japanese mustard, for serving

Notes: Ramen noodles are often available at stores with well-stocked Asian sections, usually in the refrigerator or freezer section (they're sometimes sold alone, and sometimes sold with a soup flavor pack included). If you can't find ramen noodles, you can substitute yakisoba or soba noodles; the dish won't be the same, but it'll still be tasty. Alternatively, you can transform angel hair pasta into a worthy ramen substitute using Daniel's method.

Make-ahead and storage: The noodles and toppings can be prepared hours ahead of time. Simply refrigerate and assemble when ready to serve.
author: Shao Z.
